subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Nudging Medication Adherence
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Nudging Medication Adherence.

hook.text: Half of patients with chronic conditions don't take their meds as prescribed. The pills are there. The habit isn't.

buildup.text: Daily reminder texts, pill organizers, and simplified dosing schedules are nudges that boost adherence by up to 30%.

discovery.text: Volpp used lotteries: patients eligible for daily prizes if they took their meds had 40% higher adherence.

twist.text: The lottery prize was small ($100/month), but the daily anticipation kept medication salient.

climax.text: Medication adherence nudges save lives and billions in hospital costs. Small design changes prevent big health failures.

punchline.text: A text reminder can save a life.

quiz.question: How did lottery incentives improve medication adherence?
options: Daily anticipation of winning kept medication top of mind
Patients were penalized for missing doses
